evidence: The active-duration slider writes through providerService.setAvailability(id, true, hours) on every change and invalidates the provider cache, so the duration is stored, not just displayed.
Saving working timing calls invalidateQueryCache(`provider:<id>`, () => bustProviderGetCache(id)) and refetches, so the console and the public profile agree.

Service radius lives with the rest of the provider's profile (serviceRadiusKm, used by the dashboard's find-work feed and the public listing), not on the availability screen — availability answers 'when', the profile answers 'how far'.
The toast computes whether the turn-off time is on another date (isTomorrow) and only then says 'tomorrow'.
Date and slot blocks are in the jobs console (ProviderJobs renders BlockSlotModal and the day timetable), which is where a provider also sees what a block affects.
Pending hour edits are saved before the availability toggle acts (the same isDirty guard as the business hours editor, HRS-4), so toggling can't discard them.
grep '#fff' in ProviderAvailability.tsx: none (2026-09-16).
Every catalog write busts the cached provider row (bustProviderGetCache) and the console subscribes to provider_packages for live updates, so console and storefront agree.
Deleting a service opens a confirmation sheet naming it — the provider console is the same CatalogManager the business console uses (CAT-2).
updateCatalogItem and deleteCatalogItem select the affected rows and throw when nothing was written, so a write RLS refuses is reported instead of looking like success.
The shared item editor sends explicit nulls for a cleared sale price or image, so they can be removed (CAT-1).
CatalogManager renders ProviderManageNav when kind === 'provider'.
uploadService throws instead of writing a base64 data URL when storage refuses (E2E-015).

Tiered packages and a duration attribute change what a service is, and the booking sheet, slot maths and payment amounts all read the current shape. A v1.1 product change, deferred under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
Manual ordering needs a sort column on catalog_items and a drag handle — the same change as the business catalog (CAT-3). Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The file input is cleared after each pick (e.target.value = ""), so the same file can be chosen again after a failed upload.
A CALL lead dials when the customer shared their number (provider_leads, 20260972, returns the phone only then) and otherwise opens their profile, so the card always leads somewhere.

A MESSAGE lead opens (or creates) the thread with that customer through useMessageUser instead of navigating to /chats?uid=… — a query string the conversation list never read (same root cause as E2E-041).
The inbox reads through useQueryWithRealtime on leads, so a new reachout appears without a refresh.
markLeadHandled selects the updated row and throws when nothing was written; the screen reverts its optimistic tick and shows the message.
A handled reachout shows Undo, which clears the flag (markLeadHandled(id, false)) and puts it back in the list.
Handled rows dim to 0.6 opacity and lose their action, so the unhandled ones read as the live list; with an Undo to bring one back.
The 'Mark handled' control is 44px inside the tappable card, so ticking one off no longer opens it instead.

The provider console gains a Reachouts tile (new 'inbox' capability, wired in consoleSteps and ConsoleTile) showing how many are waiting and opening /provider/:id/manage/inbox — the screen was routed but nothing in the app linked to it.
The empty state now reads per role: 'Calls and messages from customers appear here' for a provider, questions only for a business.
providerService.analytics and earningsLedger read appointments (payment_amount / package_price, fixed in E2E-006), so booking earnings are in the summary and the ledger.
The custom QR is saved on the provider row (providerService.update upiQrUrl) and read from there first; localStorage is only a same-device fallback, and clearing removes both.

Cash taken in person is recorded from the jobs console through appointment_record_walk_in_payment (the same Record payment action the business console has, BUSINESS_APPOINTMENTS B2 / PROVIDER_JOBS P3).
Saving a UPI id, a QR or a deposit percentage busts the cached provider row and invalidates provider:<id>.
saveUpi refuses anything that isn't name@handle shaped, with 'Please enter a valid UPI ID (e.g. name@bank)'.

The earnings ledger counts booking payments as well as settlements, so it is refetched whenever the appointments subscription delivers a change — subscribing to settlements alone left a cash payment recorded on a job invisible until a manual refresh.
The deposit percentage is clamped to 0–100 and rounded before saving (Math.max(0, Math.min(100, …))).
The money screen's actions are full-width buttons and rows; the small elements left are avatars and dividers, not touch targets.
The provider portfolio console filters out synthetic fallback items by id prefix (pp_def_, mock_), so only the provider's own rows can be captioned or deleted.
Delete opens a confirmation sheet (confirmDeleteItem) and the controls are 40px.
add/update/delete all bust the cached provider row, so the hub and the public profile follow immediately.
updatePortfolio and deletePortfolio select the affected rows and throw when nothing was written.
uploadService throws instead of storing a base64 data URL (E2E-015).
The caption editor has a cancel control that closes it without saving.

Testimonials would be a second kind of portfolio entry (text with an attributed author) needing its own table and moderation; reviews already carry customer voice on the profile. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
portfolio_items has sort_order and nothing ordered by it; both provider reads now order the joined portfolio by sort_order ascending, so the gallery is stable instead of following heap order.
Every portfolio control is 40px; the screen uses theme tokens (no colour literals).
providerService.submitVerification busts the cached provider row, so the hub and dashboard read the new UNDER_REVIEW state.
ProviderVerification renders ProviderManageNav.
The dashboard's verify tile reads verificationStatus: 'Under review ⏳' while pending, 'Action needed ⚠️' when rejected, and counts as done while under review.
The shared VerificationPanel refuses a PDF over 5 MB when it's picked, naming the file (VER-3).

Same reasoning as the business side (VER-4): submitted KYC documents aren't re-displayed and withdrawing a review needs an admin-side state change. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The panel takes entityType and resolves the service and its copy per role (businessService vs providerService), so a solo provider isn't asked for shop paperwork.
The status banners use theme tokens — no colour literals in VerificationPanel.tsx (2026-09-16).
